one_sentence_story: Sharp eyes can read tiny print yet fail to know your own face in a mirror. When the face hub breaks, one spoken word brings the name back.
so_what_for_you: One in fifty adults misses faces outside work or home. Say your name warmly when you meet coworkers on the weekend.

jargon_map.plain: Close friends look like strangers by face alone. Sight and memory still work fine.
jargon_map.analogy: Like seeing clear letters in a script you cannot read.

jargon_map.plain: A patch under the right side of the brain that links a whole face to one person.
jargon_map.analogy: Like the face lock sensor on a phone.

jargon_map.plain: Your palm sweats at a spouse photo even when the face looks new to you.
jargon_map.analogy: Like your heart knowing home when the street sign is gone.

jargon_map.plain: The flip side of face blindness. You know a spouse's face, yet feel zero gut warmth.
jargon_map.analogy: Like finding your house key when it will not turn the lock.
